verbs.name: screen_record.doctor
verbs.description: Report the SCREEN RECORDER's capability cards (the recorder analog of system.doctor). It also projects the app-local microphone choice: `microphones` contains only short-lived opaque tokens plus generic category-and-ordinal labels, and `microphone_selection` reports System Default, a ready selected source, or an unavailable saved source. Windows and macOS enumerate native endpoint identities privately; Linux is System Default only. No endpoint ID, UID, vendor/friendly name, serial, backend name, auth, or path is public. `warm_mic:true` opens the currently resolved source only for one bounded test; it does not persist or switch a source. No project required.

warm_mic.description: When true, briefly test the current resolved microphone source. It never changes selection, persists a token, opens a competing stream during recording, or returns a native endpoint identity.

verbs.result: {cards, ready, start_allowed, monitors:[{id?,index,name,width,height,primary}], windows:[{id,title,app?}], window_capture_supported:boolean, camera:{supported,devices:[{id,label,state,detail}],detail}, scenes:{supported,catalog_revision,layouts,timers,timer_actions,camera_required_layouts,recovery,detail}, pause:{supported,layouts?,streams?,requires?,incompatible,recovery?,detail}, quality:{supported,output_sizes,profiles,detail}, microphones:[{token,label}], microphone_selection:{mode:"system_default"|"selected",label?,status}, mic_warm?} — scenes is passive/path-free and opens no device; Presenter PiP readiness is conditional on an explicitly selected camera. pause is a passive capability: macOS may advertise the bounded exact-display/integer-FPS screen plus optional mic/system-audio owner and its current incompatibility reasons; it never opens a device and Linux/Windows advertise supported:false. camera enumeration is passive and never opens a device or permission prompt; ids are opaque and labels are display-only. A selected camera is used only by the explicit screen_record.start{camera_id} action. `quality.supported` is true only when this compiled backend owns and final-verifies simple Source/1080p/720p plus Standard/High output requests; its lists are empty otherwise and callers must omit `screen_record.start.quality`. `window_capture_supported` reports whether the compiled native backend can capture application windows, even when the current window list is empty; Linux portal capture reports false. Windows/macOS window rows carry an opaque live native `windows[].id`; the UI passes the selected id unchanged and capture revalidates it, while title and app remain display-only. Windows/macOS monitor rows include an opaque versioned native `id` only when an exact native identity is available; no surrogate is generated. Pass that `id` unchanged as `screen_record.start.monitor_id` to require a fresh exact revalidation; display name, ordinal, primary status, and dimensions never replace it. The legacy display picker continues to use only `index` when `id` is absent; Linux returns no in-app monitor rows. microphones are generic category-and-ordinal labels and expiring opaque tokens only. microphone_selection status is ready, unavailable, system_default_only, or recovered_corruption. A saved selected source that is absent remains unavailable and blocks mic-enabled start; it never falls back. mic_warm is present only when requested and tests the resolved source. No native endpoint ID/UID, vendor/friendly name, serial, backend name, auth, monitor device path, or filesystem path is returned.

verbs.name: screen_record.system_audio_probe
verbs.description: Run one explicit, bounded native system-audio delivery and signal test without starting screen capture or creating a project. This is the consenting counterpart to passive screen_record.doctor: it opens the platform loopback/process-tap path for 0.5–5 seconds, so macOS may show the separate Audio Capture permission prompt. The caller should play a sound during the window. Captured samples are held only long enough to distinguish packet delivery from an all-silent route; Linux/Windows use an exclusively-created private temporary WAV that is removed before return, macOS keeps samples in memory, and no audio bytes or path are returned. No project required.

max_ms.description: Native audio test window in milliseconds (default 2500). This bounds capture after platform activation; the action also has a fail-closed 17-second total worker timeout.

verbs.result: {supported, live, signal_detected, backend, window_ms, first_packet_offset_ms, sample_frames, detail} — live is true only when the native backend delivered a real nonempty packet during the bounded window; signal_detected is separately true only when captured samples cross the conservative -60 dBFS signal threshold. first_packet_offset_ms is measured from probe start. No captured audio or temporary path is returned or retained. An unavailable/permission-denied backend returns an actionable error or supported:false; no packet or an all-silent route returns a retry instruction and never shows green readiness.

verbs.name: screen_record.recovery_status
verbs.description: Read the durable, project-local crash-recovery status for screen recordings without starting recovery work. It returns only filesystem-safe capture ids, checkpoint/open state, and receipt facts (recovered segment count, exact-or-unknown lost-tail bounds, optional audio first-packet offset, and a source basename). It never exposes cache paths, accepts no arbitrary manifest path, and never probes media, remuxes, repairs, renames, signals, or kills a process. Requires an open project. Use this after project.open or screen_record.start recovery_scan to inspect the durable state after navigation.

after.description: Exclusive capture-id cursor returned as next_cursor. It must exactly match an emitted capture id for this project; unknown ids are rejected and it is never treated as a path.

verbs.result: {captures:[{capture_id, state:"complete"|"recovered"|"quarantined"|"interrupted"|"owner_ambiguous"|"torn_journal"|"corrupt", checkpoints, has_open_segment, receipt?:{state:"complete"|"recovered"|"quarantined"|"interrupted", recovered_segments, lost_tail_ms|null, lost_tail_lower_bound_ms, lost_tail_upper_bound_ms|null, audio_first_packet_offset_ms|null, source|null}}], next_cursor|null} — lexical project-local pagination. source is only a basename; no status row contains an absolute path or can trigger recovery.

verbs.name: screen_record.start
verbs.description: Start one LIVE screen capture in the background (in-process recorder). OPEN-ENDED: when `duration_ms` is OMITTED the capture runs UNTIL screen_record.stop is called (no fixed window — 'record until I stop'); when `duration_ms` IS given it is an optional UPPER BOUND (whichever fires first — the deadline or stop — ends the capture). A simple `quality` request is accepted only when the current `screen_record.doctor.quality.supported` capability says so; that backend records final verified dimensions, cadence, and encoder facts in the stop result, while unsupported backends refuse rather than silently ignore it. A second active capture returns conflict until the first capture and its audio worker finish. Required screen_record.doctor cards are checked before any worker starts; unavailable platform dependencies return not_found instead of an asynchronous failed recording. On Windows, the action preflights its exact compact WGC checkpoint output before any capture marker or worker: when it would exceed 260 UTF-16 code units including its terminator, it returns invalid_args synchronously with an instruction to use a shorter project path. On Linux, the action-specific preflight allows only the exact prompt-deferred XDG ScreenCast `screen_capture:unknown` card to reach the user-selected source picker; it never changes Doctor `ready`, and every missing, degraded, or other unknown required card still returns not_found. Before it reserves a new capture it scans prior project-local checkpoint manifests: only a dead owner with a contiguous independently playable finalized prefix is recovered, while live/ambiguous owners are deferred and corrupt journals fail closed. The capture runs on a background thread that, when it ends, writes project.json (a RecordingProject {settings, source_video, audio?, events}) + the source mp4 (+ a mic wav when `audio`, + system.wav when `system_audio`) under <project>/cache/screen_record/<capture_id>/. On Windows, system.wav starts at the first real WASAPI packet and a sibling system-audio.json sidecar {schema:'shellx-cut/system-audio-timing/1', first_packet_offset_ms} records its offset from capture start (null means no packet); older/no-sidecar captures retain zero-offset placement. An external stop flag is registered under capture_id so screen_record.stop can end the recording promptly. A local <dir>/.capture.json recovery marker {pid, duration_ms, open_ended, fps, audio, keys} is atomically published so screen_record.stop still recovers a completed capture even across a cutd restart (the in-memory stop flag is lost on restart, but a capture that finalized on its own bound is still read from the file). Marker metadata never selects an output path: stop always derives the exact local <capture_id>/project.json. cutd's OWN environment (WAYLAND_DISPLAY / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR / DBUS) reaches the recorder's ScreenCast portal. `window`, when set on Windows/macOS, must be the opaque identity from the latest doctor enumeration and is revalidated exactly; titles are display-only and a vanished target fails explicitly. `monitor_id`, when set, must be the opaque identity from a current doctor monitor row and is revalidated exactly before capture; it never falls back to `monitor`, name, primary state, or dimensions. `monitor` remains the compatible ordinal path when monitor_id is omitted. Capture state is filesystem-based (no AppState change). Optional expected_project_identity must equal the exact path-free project.state.project_identity under the project-transition lock; a closed project returns no_project and a switched project returns conflict before rehearsal cleanup, native admission, marker, or reservation. Requires an open project.

duration_ms.description: OPTIONAL upper-bound capture length in ms. OMIT for OPEN-ENDED capture ('record until I stop' — ended only by screen_record.stop). When given, the capture ends at this deadline OR at stop, whichever comes first.

output_size.description: Simple final-output height policy. source preserves captured dimensions; 1080p and 720p downscale only, never upscale. Accepted only when screen_record.doctor.quality.supported is true.

profile.description: Simple output-quality preset. Numeric codec controls are not part of this request.

audio.description: Also record the microphone (voice narration) → a mic wav muxed at render time (default false).

keys.description: Record keystrokes for the key-cast overlay. OFF by default (privacy: keys can reveal passwords/secrets). Opt-in.

monitor.description: 1-based monitor index to capture (Windows/macOS; from screen_record.doctor.monitors). None / 0 = primary. This legacy path is used only when monitor_id is omitted; ignored when `window` is set.

monitor_id.description: Opaque exact native identity copied unchanged from a current screen_record.doctor.monitors[].id row (Windows/macOS). It is revalidated against fresh native enumeration before capture; a stale or unavailable identity fails explicitly, with no ordinal, display-name, primary-state, or geometry fallback. Mutually exclusive with `window`. Omit it when Doctor did not provide an id.

expected_project_identity.description: Optional exact path-free identity from the current project.state.project_identity. If the open project changed or closed, Start refuses under the project-transition lock before rehearsal cleanup, native device admission, marker creation, or capture reservation. Omit only when the caller does not need project binding.

window.description: Opaque live native identity from the latest screen_record.doctor.windows[].id enumeration (Windows/macOS). It is revalidated exactly at capture start; title text never selects a target, and a malformed, closed, or replaced target fails explicitly. Takes precedence over `monitor`. Omit for the whole monitor/screen.

camera_id.description: Opaque camera id copied unchanged from the current screen_record.doctor.camera.devices list. Supplying it is the explicit Use camera action: the screen-owned native sidecar may request OS camera permission or device access after the shared CaptureClock opens, waits for a real first frame, and at terminal Stop can publish a separately editable CameraArtifact. A Start acknowledgement alone does not prove camera frames or output. Omit it to record screen only. Available only when current Doctor advertises a supported native camera build and the selected device.

scenes.description: Bounded RecordingSceneConfig@1: named Screen or Presenter PiP layouts and exactly one capture-wide off, elapsed, or countdown timer. Presenter PiP needs a selected admitted camera only when it is initial or activated live.

mode.description: Opt in to the bounded macOS pause-safe owner. It requires an exact current display and integer FPS, owns screen plus optional mic/system audio only, and rejects Scenes, camera, keys, window capture, and quality selection before capture reservation. Unavailable on Linux and Windows.

system_audio.description: Also capture DESKTOP/SYSTEM audio (game/app sound) as a separate track. Linux uses the native PipeWire default-sink monitor and measures its first nonempty packet on the capture clock; a finalized no-packet WAV is null-timed and skipped, while a PipeWire failure removes its partial WAV. Windows uses endpoint-independent process loopback; macOS uses a Core Audio process tap alongside ScreenCaptureKit.

studio.description: Optional initial Recording Studio metadata such as the chosen background. Timed camera visibility/transform changes are written through screen_record.studio_event so the raw camera take stays separately editable while polish can replay the chosen composition.

verbs.result: {capture_id, out_dir, status:"recording", duration_ms, open_ended, cadence, scenes:{enabled,saved:true,scene_id,preset_revision,catalog_revision,logical_media_time_ms:0,timer_started:false,timer,scene}|null, pause:{enabled}, studio_events, recovery_scan:{recovered:[capture_id], deferred:[detail], failed_closed:[detail]}, note} — scenes.saved acknowledges only the durable frozen journal header/config before the native CaptureClock/timer or camera has started; it is not a live timer/camera claim. pause.enabled only acknowledges opt-in admission; use screen_record.pause or screen_record.resume and their saved durable state acknowledgement before changing the UI. capture_id names a dir under <project>/cache/screen_record/; duration_ms is null + open_ended true for an open-ended capture; cadence is CaptureCadence@1 {schema, requested:{num,den}, backend_requested:{num,den}, probed_media?}, where requested is the exact reduced decimal request and backend_requested is the current v1 nearest-integer 1..240 backend request; start has no measured media facts. studio_events points at the capture's timed composition metadata; recovery_scan reports only this pre-start pass, so query screen_record.recovery_status for durable per-capture receipts; the note flags the one-time XDG ScreenCast consent dialog on the first capture. no_project if no project is open; conflict if expected_project_identity names a different open project; invalid_args if a Windows project path exceeds the WGC checkpoint limit; not_found if required recorder dependencies are unavailable; conflict if another capture still owns the recording devices.

verbs.name: screen_record.stop
verbs.description: Finalize a capture started by screen_record.start and surface its artifacts. This STOPS the capture — it sets the capture's external stop flag (ending an OPEN-ENDED recording promptly), then waits for the recorder to write its project.json and reads it. A public Recording Scenes take publishes its create-only recording-scene.receipt.json before project.json becomes visible; Stop revalidates the receipt's capture identity, terminal replay, and exact source/project SHA-256 commitments before returning or forwarding it. For a closed native checkpoint with fewer delivered frames than its measured capture span, finalization materializes the missing span as cloned video frames; contradictory timing remains a fail-closed error. Pipeline: (1) resolve <project>/cache/screen_record/<capture_id>/ (missing → not_found); (1b) SIGNAL stop so an open-ended capture ends now (no-op if cutd restarted and lost the in-memory flag — the file poll still recovers a capture that finalized on its own bound); (2) read local marker duration plus the durable journal start only to derive the exact local <capture_id>/project.json and a finite finalization budget; legacy marker project_path values are ignored; (3) POLL for project.json to exist AND be non-empty for twice the declared/observed capture work plus 15s (45s minimum, 15min maximum; 300ms between checks); never appears → a clean timeout; (4) parse the RecordingProject → extract source_video, audio?, and the embedded events EventTrack, writing the events object to <dir>/events.json (pretty) so it feeds the existing screen_record.autoedit {track} verb; (5) if autoedit:true, chain screen_record.autoedit with the finalized capture settings.fps as config.out_fps and the explicit validated scene_receipt when present, so the plan preserves recorded elapsed time. Requires an open project.

capture_id.description: The capture id returned by screen_record.start (names a dir under <project>/cache/screen_record/).

autoedit.description: After finalizing, chain screen_record.autoedit on the events track to produce an EditPlan with the finalized capture FPS as out_fps (default false).

mux_raw.description: RAW CAPTURE mode (default false): after finalizing, fold the capture's video + captured sound sources (mic + system) into ONE standalone raw.mp4 with NO autoedit/zoom/cursor/polish pass, and return it as `raw_path`. Both mic and system present → amix into a single full-level audio track. Pair with autoedit:false for Raw mode; combine with autoedit:true to save this unedited MP4 and also return an editable plan for the later polish step.

raw_path.description: Explicit raw recording .mp4 output path (FENCED). Default: the session output dir (project.set_output_dir) or <project>/exports/raw_recording.mp4.

verbs.result: {capture_id, held_last_frame_ms, project, source, audio, webcam, camera_artifact, cadence, quality, events, studio_events, scene_receipt, raw_streams, plan, clicks, cursor_samples, cursor_correlation, input_hook} — held_last_frame_ms is the measured duration filled by holding the last verified screen frame when WGC delivered zero new frames for a final checkpoint (0 for an ordinary checkpoint capture, null for unavailable legacy journal); these are generated frames, not newly captured screen pixels. project = the finalized project.json path; source = the captured source_video; audio = the mic wav path or null; webcam = the legacy-compatible optional camera path; camera_artifact = CameraArtifact@1 when a validated synchronized camera artifact exists ({schema, capture_id, artifact_id, video: relative capture leaf, clock:{first_frame_offset_ms,end_frame_offset_ms}, media:{width,height,fps_num,fps_den,frame_count,duration_ms,sha256}, terminal_state}), else null; cadence is the optional persisted CaptureCadence@1. Its optional probed_media records only successful final FFprobe facts: avg_frame_rate and r_frame_rate are exact reduced rationals, and decoded_video_frames/duration_ms are independently measured. `quality` is CaptureQualityResolution@1 {schema,requested:{output_size,profile},width,height,encoder} only when a supporting backend accepted the request and the same final verification measured an H.264 source; it is null for unsupported or legacy capture paths. Invalid 0/0 rates, failed probes, and legacy projects return cadence null or omit probed_media; no value is inferred from settings.fps. events = the written events.json path (feeds screen_record.autoedit); studio_events = the timed composition metadata path when present; scene_receipt is recording-scene.receipt.json when this take has a validated public RecordingSceneProjection@1, otherwise null; raw_streams lists discovered screen/camera/mic/system/studio artifacts plus system_timing when the Windows WASAPI packet-offset sidecar exists; plan = the EditPlan path when autoedit:true (else null); clicks/cursor_samples = the lengths of the events arrays. cursor_correlation = {source, state: exact|approximate|unavailable, exact_clicks, approximate_clicks, unavailable_clicks, max_metadata_age_ms?, detail?}; its click counters are button transitions (press and release). Wayland evdev coordinates are approximate unless paired with fresh PipeWire cursor metadata; X11 and Windows/macOS monitor rdevin desktop coordinates are exact only after a validated capture-surface transform. Linux uses actual finalized video dimensions, and marks rdevin input unavailable if they cannot be established. Windows/macOS Window clicks map only a fresh native button payload through admitted same-owner accepted frame geometry. Missing, stale, changed, minimized, closed or unmatched frames remain unavailable. These captures retain one native cursor without a duplicate synthetic cursor track; synthetic cursor styling remains unavailable. Exact click mapping does not establish full resized-window output coverage or arbitrary move/DPI correctness. No button transitions report unavailable rather than vacuous exactness. no_project if no project is open; not_found if the capture dir is absent; sidecar if the capture never finalized. RAW MODE adds raw_path (the standalone raw.mp4, null unless mux_raw:true) plus raw_has_mic/raw_has_system. input_hook is the capture-owned startup observation {state:unobserved|registered|unavailable, backend:unknown|rdevin_windows|rdevin_macos|rdevin_x11|wayland_evdev, capture_keys:boolean, reason:startup_failed only for unavailable}. registered means native registration acknowledgment only, not delivered input or continuing health; X11 acknowledges before entering its RECORD loop. unavailable reports observed optional rdevin startup failure and does not block saved video. Missing, legacy, private prepublished and uninterpretable observations return unobserved; Wayland evdev is explicitly unobserved. Native baked cursor pixels may remain even when mouse effects are missing. First-screen readiness, required/AlreadyActive/teardown failures and coordinate provenance are unchanged.

verbs.name: screen_record.studio_event
verbs.description: Append one timed Recording Studio composition event beside an active capture. During recording, camera visibility and transform events change the polished output; a camera reset event with no layout fields clears the chosen position/size/shape so the active frozen scene preset applies again. Later scene activations keep the chosen layout until reset. Recording markers are also supported. Events are metadata only: raw streams stay unbaked, and polish can replay the event stream into the EditPlan webcam timeline. Requires an open project and a capture_id returned by screen_record.start.

capture_id.description: The capture id returned by screen_record.start.

source.description: Event source. V1 supports camera composition and recording markers.

kind.description: camera+visibility toggles the camera, camera+transform changes placement/size/shape, camera+reset restores the active scene layout without changing visibility, recording+marker adds a timed marker, background+style changes the polished backdrop.

visible.description: Camera visibility for camera visibility events.

x.description: Camera overlay top-left X as a normalized output-frame fraction.

y.description: Camera overlay top-left Y as a normalized output-frame fraction.

size.description: Camera overlay height/diameter as a normalized output-frame fraction.

radius.description: Rounded-rectangle corner radius in output pixels when shape is rounded_rect.

label.description: Optional marker label for recording marker events.

background.description: Polished backdrop style for background style events.

verbs.result: {studio_events, count, last_event} — studio_events is <capture>/studio-events.json, count is the event count after append, and last_event echoes the accepted event.

verbs.name: screen_record.autoedit
verbs.description: Run the recorder's AUTO-EDIT engine: a project-local EventTrack JSON (mouse/keyboard/window events captured during a screen recording) → an EditPlan JSON (the polished cut — click-zooms, speed ramps, cursor smoothing). Uses the linked record-engine in process, writing an immutable plan under <project>/cache/screen_record/ with a name derived from the source track identity and final plan bytes. Repeating identical inputs returns the same plan path; a different take or changed plan gets a separate path. `config` is an optional partial EngineConfig override (max_zoom, zoom timings, cursor/keycast tuning, out_fps, idle tuning); unknown keys are rejected. An explicit scene_receipt returned by screen_record.stop is revalidated against its capture source/project bytes, then replays the bounded public scene timeline into the editable plan. Requires an open project (the plan is cached under it).

track.description: Project-local path to the EventTrack JSON (normally the events path returned by screen_record.stop).

config.description: Optional partial record-engine EngineConfig override. Supported keys: max_zoom, zoom_in_ms, zoom_hold_min_ms, zoom_out_ms, dwell_merge_ms, stay_zoomed_gap_ms, cursor_window, keycast_gap_ms, keycast_hold_ms, out_fps, idle_threshold_ms, enable_idle. Unknown keys are rejected.

webcam.description: Optional project-local path to the captured webcam stream. When present with studio_events, autoedit patches the EditPlan webcam overlay/timeline.

camera_artifact.description: Optional internal CameraArtifact@1 from screen_record.stop. It preserves the shared CaptureClock first/end frame interval in the generated webcam overlay plan; callers must not synthesize it from device enumeration.

studio_events.description: Optional project-local path to studio-events.json. Camera events are converted into EditPlan.webcam.timeline for polish replay.

scene_receipt.description: Optional explicit path to the capture-owned recording-scene.receipt.json returned by screen_record.stop. It must share the EventTrack's capture directory and validates the capture id, sealed public replay, terminal scene, source SHA-256, and project SHA-256 before its editable timeline is applied.

verbs.result: {plan, summary, config, studio_events, webcam, camera_clock, scene_receipt} — plan = the written EditPlan path; summary = the auto-edit plan summary; config = the resolved EngineConfig used to generate the plan; studio_events/webcam echo the optional Studio inputs when applied; camera_clock is the optional validated CameraArtifact@1 first/end frame interval retained in the webcam overlay plan; scene_receipt echoes the explicit validated receipt whose bounded scene_timeline was persisted in the plan, else null.

verbs.name: screen_record.polish
verbs.description: The recorder polish pipeline: bake the project-local recorder MP4 (source recording + EditPlan → zoom/speed/cursor polish) and DROP IT ONTO THE TIMELINE. ORCHESTRATOR (like assemble.broll / import.otio): records NO op of its own — wraps the work in an auto-checkpoint and dispatches media.import + edit.add_track + edit.insert as real, replay-safe ops. Pipeline: (1) CONTENT-ADDRESSED bake (the matte pattern) — cache key = source content hash + plan-bytes hash, baked mp4 at <project>/cache/screen_record/<key>.mp4; a hit returns cached:true and skips the bake, a miss renders through the integrated Cut recorder; (2) media.import the baked mp4 and wait for its import chain; (3) ensure the target track exists (default "v1"; an explicit absent `track` is created as a video track) then edit.insert at `at_ms` (default 0, no ripple). When the source capture directory contains a validated CameraArtifact@1, polish additionally imports its contained camera media onto a separate hidden v_camera video track at first_frame_offset_ms, with an explicit source range limited to the measured camera duration. It is editable but hidden to prevent duplicating the legacy baked webcam bubble until B7 adds the real visible-track/preview workflow. A sibling system.wav is imported on its own a_system track; when system-audio.json is present, it starts at first_packet_offset_ms after `at_ms` and is trimmed to the remaining video duration. Missing sidecars retain legacy zero-offset placement. Requires an open project.

source.description: Project-local path to the source recording MP4, normally returned by screen_record.stop.

plan.description: Project-local path to the EditPlan JSON (from screen_record.autoedit).

track.description: Target video track id (default "v1"; created if absent).

at_ms.description: Timeline position to insert the baked clip (default 0).

raw.description: When true, SKIP the slow zoom/cursor/frame re-render: stream-COPY the captured video and mux the mic (near-instant) so 'stop → editable clip' is fast. The EditPlan is still required (cache-keying) but is NOT applied; run polish again without raw for the auto-zoom/cursor pass. Default false (full polish).

verbs.result: {clip_id, asset_id, camera_artifact_id?, camera_asset_id?, camera_clip_id?, camera_track_id?, camera_first_frame_offset_ms?, system_clip_id, system_warnings, baked, cached} — baked = the cached mp4 path (polished, or stream-copied when raw:true); when a validated CameraArtifact@1 is present, camera_* identifies its independently editable v_camera clip placed at its immutable shared-clock first_frame_offset_ms; system_clip_id is the independently mixable system-audio clip when one was placed; system_warnings explains a missing packet or unsafe duration. cached = whether the bake was reused. Orchestrator: no op of its own; the sub-verbs (media.import, edit.add_track, edit.insert) record the ops, all revertible via the auto-checkpoint.

verbs.name: screen_record.export
verbs.description: Queue the project-local recorder render to a FENCED file WITHOUT touching the timeline (the "give me the finished clip" export, vs. screen_record.polish which inserts it). format "mp4" (default): render to the fenced .mp4 path through the integrated Cut recorder. Sparse or variable-rate source frames are resampled to the EditPlan FPS before compositing, so a high nominal stream rate cannot duplicate frames and lengthen the planned export. For a direct recorder capture source, MP4 export validates its sibling mic.wav and system.wav artifacts, honors system-audio.json first_packet_offset_ms (or omits a null-timed no-packet system stream), and mixes them through the planned renderer; it never falls back to an unfenced raw-path mux. format "gif": render to a temp mp4 then convert to the fenced .gif (gif_fps default 15, gif_width default 720; the temp mp4 is removed). The immediate response captures the output lease and returns a job_id; poll jobs.status for the finished file, progress, cancellation, or actionable error. The output path is fenced and an explicit `path` must match format, else the session output dir (project.set_output_dir), else <project>/exports/recording.<ext>. Requires an open project (for the fence root).

source.description: Project-local path to the source recording MP4, normally returned by screen_record.stop.

plan.description: Project-local path to the EditPlan JSON (from screen_record.autoedit).

path.description: Explicit output path matching format (.mp4 or .gif; fenced). Default: the session output dir or <project>/exports/recording.<ext>.

format.description: mp4 (default) = the polished video; gif = render then convert to an animated GIF.

gif_width.description: GIF width px (default 720, height auto; format:"gif" only).

expected_origin_path_sha256.description: Optional canonical project origin digest from project.state.project_identity; a changed project conflicts before export admission.

verbs.result: {job_id, path, format, status:"queued"} — the fenced destination is reserved before this response returns. Poll jobs.status(job_id): done.result = {path, format, frames, elapsed_ms}; failed.error is actionable. invalid_args on an unknown format.
